title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the base case of Grothendieck's construction of the 'S_0' Teichmüller groupoid S_0T_G attached to an MD-graph G (a dual graph of a degenerate curve) of modular dimension 0. In that case every vertex is a trinion (P^1 with three special points), so the stratum is a point. Notation:
- G^b is the 'broken' graph: the disjoint union over vertices s∈S of one-vertex graphs G^b_s with half-edge sets \vec Â_s (three each).
- From the previous pages, S_0T_{G^b} = ∏_s S_0T_{0,Â_s}. For a 3-element set I, S_0T_{0,I} has as base points the cyclic orders ω(I). These are, plausibly, the two 'half-plane' tangential base points of P^1−{0,1,∞}. The local fundamental group is Z^I, generated by the boundary (tangent-vector) twists. S_I acts only externally.
- S_0T_G is obtained from S_0T_{G^b} by the homomorphism (20) Z^{\vec Â} → Z^{Â}. This sends the twist of each half-edge to the twist of the edge (or free end) it belongs to: the two sides of a glued edge give the same Dehn twist.

This page.
(21) The 'orientation' group is r(G) = r(G^b) = {±1}^S, one sign per vertex. It records the switch between the two cyclic orders at that vertex.
(23) Take the S-th power of extension (14), 0→Z →(×2) Z → Z/2 → 0. Here Z/2 = r(G^b_s), and the middle Z is generated by a 'half-turn' whose square is the generator.
Push this out along Z^S → Z^{\vec Â}, induced by the source map \vec Â → S. Vertex s goes to the sum of the generators of its three half-edges. This gives
(24) 0 → Z^{\vec Â} → E(G^b) → r(G) → 0.
Concretely, E(G^b) is Z^{\vec Â} together with, for each vertex s, an element h_s lifting −1_s with 2h_s = Σ_{a∈\vec Â_s} t_a. In words: a path from one cyclic orientation of a trinion to the opposite one, done twice, rotates each of the three boundary tangent vectors by one full turn.
(25) S_0T_{G^b} ≅ E(G^b)(ε(G^b)), where ε(G^b) = ε(G) is an r(G)-torsor of 'orientation data' (built from the ω(Â_s)). The next page makes the notation explicit:
- objects are the points of ε;
- Hom(x,y) is the fibre of E over y−x ∈ r;
- composition is addition in E.
In modern terms this is the action groupoid ε//E of E acting on the torsor ε through E → r. Its vertex groups are the kernel Z^{\vec Â}.
(26) For G itself, push (24) out along (20) Z^{\vec Â} → Z^{Â}. This gives E(G), an extension of r(G) by Z^{Â}: the edge Dehn twists plus, per vertex, a 'half-sum' h_s with 2h_s equal to the sum of the twists of the edges at s (a loop counted twice). Then S_0T_G ≅ E(G)(ε(G)) (formula (28), next page), and this can serve as the definition of S_0T_G in modular dimension 0.

Purpose. This gives an intrinsic, choice-free description of the local Teichmüller groupoid at a maximally degenerate point. It has several base points (one per choice of orientation of the trinions) and half-twist-type connecting morphisms, ready to be glued into the Teichmüller tower ('Lego').
errors: Notation is inconsistent between hat and arrow. The kernel of (24) should be Z^{\vec Â} (half-edges), and that of (26) Z^{Â} (edges and free ends). The map (20), transcribed on the previous page as Z^{Â}→Z^{Â}, must be Z^{\vec Â}→Z^{Â}.
Formula (25) as written, E(G^b)(εE(G^b)), is garbled. Per the underbrace and the next page it should read S_0T_{G^b} = E(G^b)(ε(G^b)) with ε(G^b) = ε(G).
The quotient group is written r on this page and δ on the next page (in the transcription). This is the same object.

Sign conventions are not addressed: in the mapping class group of a pair of pants, the square of a half-twist is T_c T_a^{-1} T_b^{-1}. Getting 'sum of all three twists' requires an orientation convention on boundary tangent vectors (all outgoing). This is implicit, not an error.
Numbering skips (22), probably the struck-out line at the top.

ideas.what: Local fundamental groupoid at a 0-dimensional (maximally degenerate) stratum of moduli of curves, with base points indexed by orientations (cyclic orders) of the trinions, described as an action groupoid of an extension E(G) of {±1}^S by Z^{edges} on an r(G)-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizer of a pants decomposition / local Teichmüller groupoid at maximal degeneration with tangential base points; action groupoid of an extension on a torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura (maximal degeneration); Bakalov–Kirillov (Lego-Teichmüller game); Moore–Seiberg
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the Teichmüller tower and 'Lego' gluing in genus 0 and 1 but, to my knowledge, not this explicit formula

ideas.what: Half-turn extension per trinion: an element switching the cyclic orientation whose square is the sum of the three boundary twists, obtained as the S-th power of 0→Z→2Z→Z/2→0 pushed along the source map
ideas.modern_name: Half-twist / braiding–twist relation (ribbon relation c^2 = θ_{V⊗W}θ_V^{-1}θ_W^{-1})

ideas.what: Passing from broken graph G^b to G by pushout along Z^{half-edges}→Z^{edges} (the two sides of an edge give the same Dehn twist)
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / clutching of local fundamental groups (boundary twist identification)

missed.claim: Grothendieck gives a fully intrinsic, base-point-free model of the local Teichmüller groupoid at a maximally degenerate point: S_0T_G = E(G)(ε(G)), the action groupoid of a canonical extension E(G) of {±1}^S by Z^{edges} on an orientation torsor. It is built functorially by pushing out powers of 0→Z→Z→Z/2→0 along the source map and then along the half-edge→edge map. The literature (Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov) contains the same content but usually with chosen base points and presentations, not this canonical extension/torsor formalism. Novelty is in the formulation rather than the mathematics.
missed.quote: (24) 0 → Z^{\vec Â} → E(G^b) → r(G) → 0 (ne dépendant que de G^b) ... (26) ... déduite de E(G^b) (24) par l'hom (20)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A canonical torsor-level description is what one needs for Galois/GT actions on the Teichmüller tower without choosing tangential base points. It could streamline the comparison of GT-actions at different maximal degenerations.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, intrinsic packaging of the local groupoid at maximal degeneration, including the half-turn extension with 2h_s = Σ boundary twists, dating from around 1978–84. That predates Nakamura's and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps's treatments. The mathematical content is now well known, though, so only the early date and the canonical formalism are notable.
